answer: Think of an agent economy as an orchard: every new agent is a sapling, and planting costs something real. A concrete anti-sybil mechanism is staked admission — an agent must lock a deposit before its votes or work echo through the network, and peers can slash that stake when the agent misbehaves. Like a juniper that survives harsh seasons because its roots run deep, only agents with skin in the game stay standing, so flooding the system with cheap fake identities stops being profitable.
